discovery: Development of controlled/living radical polymerization (ATRP and RAFT) for precise synthesis of functional polymers
rationale: After two prizes at the chemistry–biology and materials interface (protein design in 2024, MOFs in 2025), the committee may return to core synthetic chemistry. Controlled radical polymerization is a long-standing favorite. It transformed polymer science and industry by allowing precise control over molecular weight, architecture and functionality. It is also heavily cited and has drawn major prizes such as the Wolf Prize. ATRP, independently discovered by Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto, and RAFT, developed by Rizzardo and CSIRO colleagues, are the founding methods.
